rationale: This is a cosmetic lag-plus-broadening variant of the archived "Debt-Funded Payout Deficit" (dltis × payout-minus-oancf, fmb −3.03, alpha −0.046) and closely overlaps "External Payout Funding Shortfall," and with annual data a one-year lag of a highly persistent payout-shortfall ratio adds little independent information.

Both multiplied terms are monotonically increasing in gross issuance, so the product is largely a rescaled restatement of the well-documented external-financing/net-issuance anomaly rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction, and it duplicates the archive's existing gross-financing-vs-cash-flow family.

Inserting debt service into the bounded payout-coverage residual is an economically motivated seniority refinement that combines two archive signals with partial support (payout coverage fmb 1.74; oancf/dltr fmb 2.30, alpha 0.040) and is internally consistent with the positive expected sign, though it remains an incremental extension rather than a new mechanism.

target_name: Successful Term-Out of Prior Liquidity Stress
rationale: The triple condition (issuance, falling current liabilities, prior working-capital deficit) is a coherent and internally consistent test of successful maturity extension that differs in construction from the archived "Failed Maturity Refinance" (lct rather than dlc, lagged deficit, positive sign), but it risks simply recovering the mirror image of that already-evaluated signal.

This is the archived "Dual-Market Distress Funding" (fmb −2.93, alpha −0.045, t −3.11) with a single one-year lag applied to a highly autocorrelated oancf/at term — a near-exact rediscovery whose economic content is essentially unchanged.

The net-debt-issuance × sales-contraction pairing is already the long leg of the archived "Debt-Demand Mismatch Spread" (fmb −1.94), and swapping MIN for MUL plus a one-year lag is an aggregator/timing tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism.
